title: DevSecOps Best Practices & Tools 🛠️
description: SAST, DAST, IAST, and building a continuous security feedback loop.

slides.title: Beyond SAST: A Complete Testing Arsenal 🧪
slides.content:
# Cover Every Angle

| Method | What It Does | When It Runs |
|--------|--------------|--------------|
| **SAST** (Static) | Analyzes source code for patterns | Build, IDE |
| **DAST** (Dynamic) | Scans running application like an attacker | Test, Staging |
| **IAST** (Interactive) | Agent inside the app monitors real traffic | Test, QA |
| **RASP** (Runtime) | Protects app in production by detecting attacks | Production |
| **SCA** (Composition) | Scans open‑source dependencies | Build |

*No single tool catches everything. Combine them for comprehensive coverage.*

quizData.question: Which testing method scans a running application from the outside, simulating a real attacker?
quizData.explanation: DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) probes a live application for vulnerabilities.

slides.title: DAST in Your Pipeline 🎯
slides.content:
## Automated Penetration Testing

- Tools: OWASP ZAP (free, open source), Burp Suite Enterprise, WebInspect.
- Run DAST against a staging environment after deployment.
- It crawls the app, sends malicious payloads, and reports vulnerabilities like XSS, SQLi.
- **Critical**: DAST can modify data or trigger side effects. Use a disposable test environment or be careful with destructive scans.

*DAST finds runtime issues that SAST cannot, like authentication bypass or misconfigured headers.*

slides.title: OWASP ZAP Baseline Scan (Docker)
slides.content: Run a quick DAST scan on your staging site:
slides.codeSnippet:
docker run -t owasp/zap2docker-stable zap-baseline.py \
  -t https://staging.example.com \
  -g gen.conf \
  -r report.html

slides.title: IAST & RASP: The Next Level 🚀
slides.content:
- **IAST (Interactive)**: An agent inside the application (e.g., Contrast Assess) observes data flow during functional testing. It pinpoints the exact line of vulnerable code with low false positives.
- **RASP (Runtime Application Self‑Protection)**: An agent that runs in production and blocks attacks in real time (e.g., SQL injection attempts). It's like a WAF inside the app.

*IAST is for testing; RASP is for defense. Both require language‑specific agents.*

slides.title: Building a Feedback Loop 🔄
slides.content:
## Security Visibility in One Place

- Send all findings (SAST, DAST, dependency scan) to a central dashboard (e.g., DefectDojo, AWS Security Hub, Azure Security Center).
- **Triage**: Assign severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low). Set SLAs for remediation (e.g., Critical fixed within 24 hours).
- **Automated tickets**: Integrate with Jira to create issues automatically.
- **Trend analysis**: Are vulnerabilities decreasing over time? Celebrate the trend.

*If security feels invisible, developers will ignore it. Make it measurable and visible.*

quizData.question: Developers should be responsible for fixing security bugs found by automated scans, not the security team.
quizData.explanation: DevSecOps means security is a shared responsibility. Developers own the fix; security team provides guidance and tools.

slides.title: Gamify Security 🎮
slides.content: Run 'bug bounty' days internally. Award points for fixing issues. Make security engineering a fun challenge, not a chore.
